A.explanation: The vertical arrow up reverses the weight and the horizontal arrow left reverses the rod push, so the loop does not match the true directions at P.

B.explanation: The vertical down can be weight and horizontal right can be the rod, but the cable arrow points down to the right, opposite to the up to the left pull of the cable on P.

C.explanation: The cable direction up to the left is correct, but the vertical up and horizontal left are opposite to the downward weight and rightward rod force on P.

D.explanation: Vertical down is the lamp weight, horizontal right is the rod pushing P away from the wall, and diagonal up to the left is the cable tension pulling P to the wall.

hints: List the three forces on point P and their true directions: lamp weight vertically down, cable tension up to the left along the cable, rod force horizontally away from the wall.
For equilibrium the three vectors placed head-to-tail must close to zero, so check which vertical and horizontal senses allow closure with an up-left cable vector.
Test the loop: start down for weight, then go across for the rod, then see which diagonal direction returns to the start.
walkthrough: Identify forces at P: $W$ of the lamp acts vertically down, tension $T$ from the cable acts on P up and to the left along the cable, and the metal rod in compression pushes P horizontally to the right.
Point P is in equilibrium, so the vector sum is zero and the three vectors drawn head-to-tail must form a closed triangle.
A closed loop needs one side straight down for $W$, one side straight across for the rod force, and one slanted side parallel to the cable for $T$.
Going round the loop, after going down for $W$ and right for the rod push, the only way back to the start is up and to the left, which is exactly the direction of the cable tension on P.
Only the triangle with vertical arrow down, horizontal arrow to the right, and hypotenuse arrow up to the left satisfies all three directions and closes head-to-tail. This is option D.
